title: The Book of Joshua Timeline
sub: Be Strong and Courageous · Choose This Day Whom You Will Serve
desc: Moses's successor leads Israel across the Jordan on dry ground, conquers Canaan city by city, divides the land among the twelve tribes, and closes with a farewell covenant renewal at Shechem.

eras.label: Era One · Joshua 1
eras.name: Be Strong and Courageous
eras.dates: Moses's successor receives a commissioning charge before a single Israelite crosses the Jordan

events.title: Be Strong and Courageous — the LORD Is With You Wherever You Go
events.detail: After Moses's death, the LORD commissions Joshua to lead Israel into Canaan, commanding him three times to be strong and courageous and to keep the law of Moses constantly on his lips, promising his presence wherever Joshua goes.

verses.text: “Be strong and courageous! Do not be terrified or dismayed, for the LORD [Yahweh] your God [Elohim] is with you wherever you go.”

eras.label: Era Two · Joshua 2
eras.name: Rahab and the Spies
eras.dates: Two spies sent secretly into Jericho are hidden by an unlikely ally whose faith becomes the reason her whole family survives

events.title: Rahab Hides the Spies — the LORD Your God Is God in Heaven and Earth
events.detail: A Canaanite prostitute named Rahab hides two Israelite spies and confesses that the LORD has already terrified all of Jericho, securing a promise of safety for her family in exchange for her loyalty — a pledge marked by a red rope tied in her window.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] your God [Elohim] is God [Elohim] in heaven above and on earth below!”

eras.label: Era Three · Joshua 3-4
eras.name: Crossing the Jordan on Dry Ground
eras.dates: The Jordan River, at flood stage, stops flowing the moment the priests carrying the ark step into it, echoing the exodus generation's crossing of the Red Sea

events.title: The Waters of the Jordan Stopped Flowing
events.detail: As soon as the priests carrying the ark of the covenant touch the flooded Jordan, the water piles up far upstream and the entire nation crosses on dry ground, honoring Joshua before Israel just as the LORD had been with Moses.

verses.text: “When the feet of the priests carrying the ark of the LORD [Yahweh], the LORD [Yahweh] of the whole earth, touch the water of the Jordan, the water coming downstream toward you will stop flowing.”

events.title: Twelve Stones as a Lasting Memorial
events.detail: Twelve stones taken from the middle of the riverbed are set up as a permanent memorial so future generations will ask what they mean and be told the story of how the LORD dried up the Jordan.

verses.text: “He has done this so all the nations of the earth might recognize the LORD's power and so you might always obey the LORD your God.”

eras.label: Era Four · Joshua 5
eras.name: Circumcision, Passover, and the Commander of the LORD's Army
eras.dates: Before any battle, the new generation is ritually consecrated, and Joshua encounters a mysterious armed figure who identifies himself not as an ally but as the LORD's own commander

events.title: Circumcision and Passover Restored at Gilgal
events.detail: The wilderness generation's uncircumcised sons are circumcised at Gilgal and the nation celebrates Passover, after which the manna that had sustained them for forty years stops entirely as they begin eating the produce of Canaan itself.

verses.text: “The manna stopped appearing the day they ate some of the produce of the land; the Israelites never ate manna again.”

events.title: I Am the Commander of the LORD's Army
events.detail: A mysterious armed figure appears to Joshua near Jericho, refusing to take sides in the coming battle because he answers to neither — he is the commander of the LORD's own army, and Joshua removes his sandals on holy ground.

verses.text: “I am the commander of the LORD's [Yahweh's] army. Now I have arrived!” Joshua bowed down with his face to the ground.

eras.label: Era Five · Joshua 6
eras.name: The Walls of Jericho Fall
eras.dates: Seven days of silent marching around a sealed city end in a shout, a collapsing wall, and total conquest — except for one household

events.title: The Wall Collapsed — Only Rahab's Household Was Spared
events.detail: After marching silently around Jericho for seven days, Israel gives a battle cry on the seventh circuit of the seventh day, and the wall collapses completely; the city is destroyed except for Rahab and her family, spared for hiding the spies.

verses.text: “Joshua told the people, ‘Shout, for the LORD [Yahweh] has given you the city!’”

eras.label: Era Six · Joshua 7
eras.name: Achan's Sin and Israel's Defeat at Ai
eras.dates: One man's secret theft from Jericho's devoted plunder brings a humiliating defeat and exposes hidden sin through a solemn process of elimination

events.title: Achan's Hidden Theft — Israel Defeated at Ai
events.detail: Unknown to Joshua, Achan secretly kept some of Jericho's devoted plunder, and Israel suffers a shocking defeat at tiny Ai as a result; a tribe-by-tribe, clan-by-clan process exposes Achan, whose confession and punishment restore the LORD's favor.

verses.text: “Achan told Joshua, ‘It is true. I have sinned against the LORD [Yahweh] the God [Elohim] of Israel.’”

eras.label: Era Seven · Joshua 8
eras.name: Ai Conquered — the Law Read at Mount Ebal
eras.dates: A carefully planned ambush finally takes Ai, and the campaign pauses for a formal covenant renewal ceremony between two mountains

events.title: An Ambush Captures Ai
events.detail: Following the LORD's specific battle plan, Joshua lures Ai's army out of the city with a feigned retreat while an ambush force captures and burns it, this time with full victory and no hidden sin to blame.

verses.text: “Then you rise up from your hiding place and seize the city. The LORD [Yahweh] your God [Elohim] will hand it over to you.”

events.title: The Law Read Aloud at Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim
events.detail: As Moses had commanded, Joshua builds an altar, inscribes a copy of the law on stones, and reads the entire law aloud, blessings and curses alike, before the whole assembly of Israel split between two mountains.

verses.text: “Joshua read aloud all the words of the law, including the blessings and the curses, just as they are written in the law scroll.”

eras.label: Era Eight · Joshua 9
eras.name: The Gibeonite Deception
eras.dates: A clever ruse tricks Israel into a treaty it cannot break, teaching a hard lesson about consulting the LORD before making commitments

events.title: The Gibeonites Trick Israel Into a Treaty
events.detail: Disguised in worn-out clothes and moldy bread to appear as distant travelers, the Gibeonites secure a peace treaty with Israel by deception; though the trick is discovered three days later, the sworn oath in the LORD's name must still be honored.

verses.text: “The men examined some of their provisions, but they failed to ask the LORD's advice.”

eras.label: Era Nine · Joshua 10
eras.name: The Sun Stands Still — the Southern Campaign
eras.dates: Defending their new allies at Gibeon, Israel wins a battle so decisive that the sun itself is said to have stood still over it

events.title: O Sun, Stand Still Over Gibeon — the LORD Fought for Israel
events.detail: Five Amorite kings attack Gibeon for making peace with Israel, and in the ensuing battle the LORD hurls hailstones on the enemy and, in an event unlike any before or since, the sun stands still to give Israel time to complete the victory.

verses.text: “There has not been a day like it before or since. The LORD [Yahweh] listened to a human being, for the LORD [Yahweh] fought for Israel!”

eras.label: Era Ten · Joshua 11-12
eras.name: The Northern Campaign — Thirty-One Kings Defeated
eras.dates: A northern coalition led by the king of Hazor meets the same fate as the south, closing with a comprehensive list of every defeated king

events.title: Hazor Burned — Joshua Conquered the Whole Land
events.detail: A northern coalition led by King Jabin of Hazor gathers at the Waters of Merom but is routed by Israel; Hazor, the former leader of these kingdoms, is the only city Israel burns, and the land finally has rest from war.

verses.text: “Joshua conquered the whole land, just as the LORD had promised Moses… Then the land was free of war.”

events.title: A Roll Call of Thirty-One Defeated Kings
events.detail: A summary chapter lists every king defeated on both sides of the Jordan, from Sihon and Og in the days of Moses to the thirty-one kings Joshua personally overthrew west of the river.

verses.text: “The king of Tirzah (one)—a total of thirty-one kings.”

eras.label: Era Eleven · Joshua 13-17
eras.name: Dividing the Land — Caleb's Request and Zelophehad's Daughters
eras.dates: The conquered territory is formally allotted tribe by tribe, punctuated by two stories of individuals who insist on receiving exactly what was promised them

events.title: The Land East of the Jordan Assigned
events.detail: Though much land remains unconquered, Joshua, now old, is told to proceed with dividing the territory, beginning with the land Moses had already assigned to Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh east of the Jordan.

verses.text: “You are very old, and a great deal of land remains to be conquered.”

events.title: Caleb Requests the Hill Country at Eighty-Five
events.detail: Caleb, now eighty-five, recalls the promise Moses made him for his faithful spy report forty-five years earlier and requests the very hill country still occupied by fearsome Anakites, trusting the LORD to help him conquer it as promised.

verses.text: “Assign me this hill country that the LORD promised me at that time… assuming the LORD is with me, I will conquer them, as the LORD promised.”

events.title: Judah's Territory — Caleb's Daughter Achsah Receives Springs of Water
events.detail: Judah's extensive tribal boundaries and cities are recorded in detail, including Caleb's daughter Achsah, who boldly asks her father for springs of water to accompany her allotted land and receives both the upper and lower springs.

verses.text: “Since you have given me land in the Negev, now give me springs of water.” So he gave her both the upper and lower springs.

events.title: Ephraim and Manasseh — Zelophehad's Daughters Receive Their Inheritance
events.detail: The territory of Ephraim and Manasseh is assigned, including land specifically given to the daughters of Zelophehad, who had no brothers, fulfilling the LORD's earlier command through Moses that daughters could inherit when a family had no sons.

verses.text: “‘The LORD told Moses to assign us land among our relatives.’ So Joshua assigned them land among their uncles, as the LORD had commanded.”

eras.label: Era Twelve · Joshua 18-19
eras.name: The Remaining Land Divided by Lot at Shiloh
eras.dates: Seven tribes still without territory are surveyed and allotted their land by lot before the assembled nation at Shiloh

events.title: How Long Will You Delay? — Seven Tribes Receive Their Land by Lot
events.detail: Joshua challenges seven still-unsettled tribes to stop delaying, has the land surveyed and mapped into seven regions, and casts lots before the LORD at Shiloh to assign the remaining territory, closing with a small parcel of land given to Joshua himself.

verses.text: “How long do you intend to put off occupying the land the LORD God of your ancestors has given you?”

eras.label: Era Thirteen · Joshua 20-21
eras.name: Cities of Refuge and Levitical Cities
eras.dates: Special cities are set aside for accidental manslaughter and for the priestly tribe that received no territorial inheritance of its own

events.title: Cities of Refuge for Accidental Manslaughter
events.detail: Six cities are designated as places of asylum where someone who accidentally killed another person could flee from the avenger of blood and receive a fair hearing before the community.

verses.text: “Anyone who accidentally kills someone can escape there; these cities will be a place of asylum from the avenger of blood.”

events.title: Not One of the LORD's Faithful Promises Was Left Unfulfilled
events.detail: The Levites, who received no land inheritance of their own, are given forty-eight cities scattered among the other tribes; the book of conquest closes with a sweeping declaration that every single promise the LORD made to Israel had now come true.

verses.text: “Not one of the LORD's [Yahweh's] faithful promises to the family of Israel was left unfulfilled; every one was realized.”

eras.label: Era Fourteen · Joshua 22
eras.name: The Altar of Witness Controversy
eras.dates: The eastern tribes head home and build a massive altar that nearly triggers civil war, until its true purpose is explained

events.title: A Reminder, Not a Rival Altar
events.detail: The Reubenites, Gadites, and half-tribe of Manasseh build an imposing altar near the Jordan on their way home, alarming the rest of Israel into preparing for war until it's explained the altar was never meant for sacrifice — only as a permanent reminder that they too belong to the LORD.

verses.text: “The Reubenites and Gadites named the altar, ‘Surely it is a Reminder to us that the LORD is God.’”

eras.label: Era Fifteen · Joshua 23-24
eras.name: Joshua's Farewell — Choose This Day Whom You Will Serve
eras.dates: An aging Joshua delivers two final speeches, the second culminating in the Old Testament's most quoted call to decisive covenant loyalty

events.title: Be Very Strong — Do Not Associate With These Nations
events.detail: Now very old, Joshua warns the assembled leaders against intermarrying or making alliances with the remaining nations, reminding them that just as every one of the LORD's promises of blessing has been fulfilled, so will every warned judgment be if they turn away.

verses.text: “Not even one of all the faithful promises the LORD your God made to you is left unfulfilled; every one was realized.”

events.title: Choose This Day Whom You Will Serve — As for Me and My House
events.detail: At Shechem, Joshua recounts the LORD's entire faithfulness from Abraham through the conquest, then issues the book's climactic challenge to choose which god to serve, closing with his own household's famous declaration of loyalty and his death at 110.

verses.text: “Choose today whom you will worship… But I and my family will worship the LORD [Yahweh].”
